findings.claim: Primary index lookup is inlined affine arithmetic, not a single function to replace. 70b17f multiplies index by0xc60;70b186 reads managed handle at Mission+0x2d68.70850a and5cd1b8 independently recreate Agent addresses. Old relocation manifests omit many primary operands because their offsets did not move.

Pool+0x629d00 holds two-byte successor/index bookkeeping, not Agent pointers. Allocator writes the object index at Agent+0x10 as32bits, reads link entries with MOVSX, and writes capacity+1 terminal sentinels. Replacing only that table with pointers will not redirect the affine consumers.

Slot2040 starts exactly at primary metadata Mission+0x62ca50. Appending an allocation or reserving addresses after a live original Mission cannot create a contiguous extension there without displacing live bookkeeping and later objects. Segments can preserve original Agent addresses only after redirecting all resolver/iterator/metadata consumers.

Managed Agent retains13 native field pointers; retained CIL finds stores only at construction/Clear. Native constructor also stores Agent self/owner/component pointers and spawn stores companion pointer at Agent+0x20. Existing raw addresses must stay stable; rewriting managed Index alone is insufficient.

Primary iterator59e54d advances a raw pointer by0xc60. Companion release5d86fa walks backwards by0x2c8. Segments need segment-aware iteration, including reverse scans, destructors, jobs and exception cleanup, not just index lookup replacement.

Unchanged signed16 metadata and capacity+1 sentinel conservatively require capacity<=32766. First live2040->4080 must rewrite terminal2041 entries before that value becomes a valid index, or replace the link representation/algorithm. Genuine unbounded-by-short segmented storage requires widening and rewriting all signed loads, stores, comparisons and helper contracts; Agent.Index remainsInt32.

Spawn indexes all three companions with the same index and retains an Agent-to-companion pointer. They require coordinated stable growth and publication. The second0xc60 pool is lifecycle-observed with unknown activation semantics; it cannot be repurposed as overflow storage merely because its sampled count is zero.

Native capacity getter is constant; managed spawn logic caches capacity and derives troop quota/2. Runtime growth requires a live admission/quota contract. Managed AgentList is expandable. Agent.Index isInt32; wire/replay descriptor is11bits(-1..2046), incompatible with4080 IDs. Single0 remains required until coordinated protocol changes.

Fresh numeric access classes include unrelated stack, image and object fields. Exact unresolved owner count is retained below. No claim that all dynamic/index arithmetic, indirect consumers, pointer subtraction/division, external modules or interior entrypoints are closed.

No proven live growth barrier yet. Constructors, linked metadata, companion state, job partitions, cached capacity and renderer requirements must be prepared before one synchronized capacity publication; failures must leave old storage, old IDs, old handles and capacity unchanged. Deletion/reuse/teardown must reject stale generation handles and destroy only constructed records once. This is a design obligation, not an observed existing engine mechanism.

architectureComparison.preserved: Existing Agent/field/companion pointers stay valid for each record lifetime; old blocks remain pinned until references retire.
architectureComparison.required: Introduce sidecar resolver and iteration contracts; rewrite every proven affine access, forward/backward stride scan, metadata algorithm and inverse pointer/index consumer. Widen link bookkeeping and add stable logical IDs plus generation handling. New blocks and all companions publish together under a proved barrier.
architectureComparison.firstGrowth: Old primary block can remain in place; new indices resolve to external blocks. Original inline metadata must be redirected or shadowed consistently, including all successor/sentinel consumers.
architectureComparison.laterGrowth: No fixed virtual reservation ceiling is needed, but existing Int32 indices, signed16 tables, packed IDs, allocation sizes, renderer/job limits and resource budgets remain distinct finite contracts until replaced.64bit sidecar handles alone do not widen engine ABIs.

architectureComparison.preserved: Affine addresses can remain stable within a reservation made before first construction.
architectureComparison.required: Reserve final regions before Mission construction and move metadata/tail layout outside potential growth spans before pointers escape. Separate reserved, committed, constructed and published capacity; adapt lifecycle and caches.
architectureComparison.firstGrowth: Cannot extend original live primary layout into its existing metadata. A newly constructed redesigned Mission can commit/construct additional records in its pre-reserved region.
architectureComparison.laterGrowth: Finite reservation budget is a ceiling. It is a useful implementation comparison or bounded prototype, not removal of the architectural limit.

lookupOffsetSubstitutionCase.registerPolicy: Preserve RCX and all non-result registers/XMM state unless independently proven dead. A C++ helper call may clobber RCX/RDX/R8/R9/R10/R11 and XMM0..5; direct insertion without a preserving stub is invalid.

findings.claim: Agent.Index and AgentCreationResult.Index are Int32. AgentHelper.GetAgentIndex directly reads a native int32 via ldind.i4; the native pool free-index table being int16 does not make the Agent object index int16.
findings.patchRequirement: Preserve int32 native object field representation and the existing managed ABI. Do not widen the object index or change struct layout merely because pool bookkeeping uses short indices.

findings.claim: Agent constructor retains 13 native pointers in fields at IL_0078 through IL_0108, calls IMBAgent.SetMonoObject at IL_0130, and AgentHelper dereferences those pointers directly. All stores found to these fields across scanned assemblies belong to Agent constructor or Agent.Clear; no relocation refresh method was found by this direct-field-reference scan.
findings.patchRequirement: Choose final pool storage before first Mission/Agent construction, keep addresses stable through deletion, and retain SetMonoObject reverse links. Reject live pool relocation; runtime patch removal must wait until all modified-layout missions are destroyed.

findings.claim: Mission.FindAgentWithIndexAux rejects only negative indices and otherwise forwards Int32 to native lookup. Managed code provides no upper bound.

limitations: Numeric candidates are not automatic rewrite authority. Exact owner-status counts deliberately preserve unresolved sites and known exclusions.

Full file-backed executable sections are covered by pdata anchored decoding plus outside-pdata linear decoding. Data islands, resynchronization, computed code and instruction overlap remain explicit limits.
Reciprocal/factorized arithmetic search is overinclusive and incomplete; it does not prove pointer-to-index semantics without data-flow ownership.
Retained managed CIL and REA evidence is reused with source hashes; no current installed assembly is read or executed.
This identifies concrete growth barriers and an actionable review queue, not a closed complete engine-consumer proof or test-ready live-growth patch.
